content:
Rumors suggest that the AirPods 5 will make their debut next week alongside the iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12, as well as the iPhone Ultra. Here's what we know so far about the new AirPods.

The AirPods 5 are expected to be unveiled at the September 9 event, available in two models, but without cameras

Apple's biggest annual event will be held next week on September 9. In addition to the new iPhone, Apple Watch models, and possibly some home products, the AirPods 5 are also expected to launch at the same time.

The AirPods 4 were released in 2024, and Apple's update cycle between successive AirPods generations has typically been two to three years. The original AirPods launched in 2016, AirPods 2 in 2019, AirPods 3 in 2021, and AirPods 4 in 2024. So based on this timeline, a release this year roughly fits the pattern.

However, somewhat surprisingly, rumors and leaks about the new AirPods have been few and far between so far.

Most of the AirPods rumors in recent months have centered around a new model with cameras. An earlier video leaked from within Apple's software showed a model equipped with cameras, leading to speculation that it would launch soon.

However, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman has said that AirPods with cameras won't arrive before 2027. But he expects the non-camera AirPods 5 to make their debut at Apple's September event. He wrote earlier:

In a further post on X, Gurman added that the AirPods 5 will come in two different models:

  • With Active Noise Cancellation (ANC)
  • Without ANC

In an earlier report, Gurman mentioned that he expects the AirPods 5 won't feature the heart rate sensor found in the AirPods Pro 3, but that Apple is "looking into adding more health features to AirPods in the future, including a body temperature sensor." He also separately mentioned that Apple is developing an "H3 chip designed to reduce latency and improve audio quality."

It remains unclear whether the AirPods 5 will adopt the H3 chip. When Apple launched the H2 chip, it was initially exclusive to the AirPods Pro lineup.

However, new health sensors could potentially make their way into the AirPods 5, and the H3 chip is also one of the possibilities. Beyond that, details about the AirPods 5 are still quite limited at this stage. Perhaps, just like with the AirPods Max 2 launched earlier this year, Apple will be able to surprise us when it unveils the AirPods 5.

What features do you want to see in Apple's next-generation AirPods? Let us know in the comments section.
